bill.title: A bill to prevent the distribution of intimate visual depictions without consent.
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

classification.plainSummary: This bill would create federal penalties for distributing intimate visual images or videos of someone without their consent. It would make it illegal to share such material if the person depicted did not agree to the distribution, addressing what is commonly known as "revenge porn" or nonconsensual pornography. The bill would establish criminal and civil remedies for victims whose private intimate images are shared without permission.

industries.rationale: Technology platforms and social media companies would face new compliance obligations around hosting and removing nonconsensual intimate imagery.
The bill creates new civil causes of action and criminal penalties, generating demand for legal services in both prosecution and defense.

method.formula: score = Σ_industries ( donorShare(industry) × billWeight(industry) ), where billWeight = classifierConfidence / Σ classifierConfidence. Range 0–1, read as a weighted share of disclosed itemized money.

ordinary.text: They wrote this bill. Sponsoring a bill about your own district's industry is the ordinary case, not the odd one.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
